rows: User profiles Hacker News reports as just changed, usually because their karma moved

rows.vgi.doc_llm: The user profiles Hacker News' change feed lists at this moment, each in its current state. A profile changes whenever its karma does, so this is a sample of whose posts are being voted on right now. A few dozen rows; for a specific person use `user()`.
rows.vgi.doc_md:
The profile half of the API's change feed, hydrated.

### A sample, not a directory

The API cannot list users; this feed and item authors are the only ways to discover usernames. It lists a few dozen recently changed profiles, turning over within minutes.

### Payload

Each row carries the user's whole `submitted` list, which for a long-standing account is thousands of ids.
rows.vgi.example_queries: [{"description": "Recently active users, by karma", "sql": "SELECT username, karma, created_at, len(submitted) AS posts FROM hackernews.main.updated_users ORDER BY karma DESC"}]
rows.vgi.title: Recently Changed Users

rows: CREATE TABLE updated_users(rank INTEGER NOT NULL, username VARCHAR, created_at TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE, karma BIGINT, about VARCHAR, submitted BIGINT[], UNIQUE(rank), PRIMARY KEY(username));
The id of the newest item on Hacker News, as a single row

rows.vgi.doc_llm: One row holding the newest item id on Hacker News. Because every story and comment takes the next id in sequence, it doubles as a running count of everything ever posted, and the difference between two readings is how much was posted in between.
rows.vgi.doc_md:
A single row, a single column.

### Uses

Ids are assigned in one sequence across all item types, so this is both the newest item and the size of the site. `recent_items()` walks back from it, which is usually the easier way to read what it points at.
rows.vgi.example_queries: [{"description": "The newest item on the site, fetched in full", "sql": "SELECT i.type, i.author, i.created_at FROM hackernews.main.max_item m, LATERAL hackernews.main.item(m.id) i"}]
rows.vgi.title: Newest Item Id

rows: CREATE TABLE max_item(id BIGINT, PRIMARY KEY(id));
Job ads from Y Combinator companies currently on the Hacker News jobs page

rows.vgi.doc_llm: The job ads currently on the site's jobs page, posted by Y Combinator companies. Each is a job item: the role is in `title`, the details in `url` or `text`. Jobs cannot be voted on or discussed, so `score` carries no signal and `descendants` is NULL. Monthly 'Who is hiring?' threads are ordinary stories, not these.
rows.vgi.doc_md:
Up to 200 job ads, as the jobs page ranks them; usually a few dozen.

### Not the hiring threads

The monthly 'Ask HN: Who is hiring?' threads, where any company can post, are stories with the ads in their comments. This list is only the ads YC companies place directly.

### Cost

Rows stream in rank order, 100 per batch and one request per story, so a `LIMIT` reads only what it returns; an `ORDER BY` reads the whole list first.
rows.vgi.example_queries: [{"description": "Current job ads, newest first", "sql": "SELECT title, url, created_at FROM hackernews.main.job_stories ORDER BY created_at DESC"}]
rows.vgi.title: Jobs

rows: CREATE TABLE job_stories(rank INTEGER NOT NULL, id BIGINT, "type" VARCHAR, author VARCHAR, created_at TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE, title VARCHAR, url VARCHAR, "text" VARCHAR, score BIGINT, descendants BIGINT, parent BIGINT, poll BIGINT, kids BIGINT[], parts BIGINT[], deleted BOOLEAN, dead BOOLEAN, UNIQUE(rank), PRIMARY KEY(id));
Show HN posts currently listed: things members have built, as the Show HN page ranks them

rows.vgi.doc_llm: The Show HN posts the site's 'show' page lists right now — projects, products and demos members have built and want feedback on. The launch link is in `url` and any write-up in `text`; the feedback is the discussion under each `id`.
rows.vgi.doc_md:
Up to 200 Show HN posts, in the ranking of the site's 'show' page.

### What counts

Show HN is for something the poster made that others can try, so this is a live sample of what people are launching. Titles start with 'Show HN:'.

### Cost

Rows stream in rank order, 100 per batch and one request per story, so a `LIMIT` reads only what it returns; an `ORDER BY` reads the whole list first.
rows.vgi.example_queries: [{"description": "The Show HN launches getting the strongest response", "sql": "SELECT title, url, score, descendants AS comments FROM hackernews.main.show_stories ORDER BY score DESC LIMIT 10"}]
rows.vgi.title: Show HN

rows: CREATE TABLE show_stories(rank INTEGER NOT NULL, id BIGINT, "type" VARCHAR, author VARCHAR, created_at TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE, title VARCHAR, url VARCHAR, "text" VARCHAR, score BIGINT, descendants BIGINT, parent BIGINT, poll BIGINT, kids BIGINT[], parts BIGINT[], deleted BOOLEAN, dead BOOLEAN, UNIQUE(rank), PRIMARY KEY(id));
Items Hacker News reports as just changed — new replies, votes, edits — in their current state

rows.vgi.doc_llm: The stories and comments Hacker News' change feed lists at this moment, each in its current state. Reach for it to see what is active right now — threads gaining replies, stories gaining votes — as opposed to what is ranked. The feed is a short rolling window of a few dozen items, so it answers 'right now', not 'today'.
rows.vgi.doc_md:
The item half of the API's change feed, hydrated.

### What a change is

The feed says only that an item changed, not how: a reply adds to `kids`, a vote moves `score`, an edit rewrites `text`. To see motion, read twice and compare on `id`.

### Size

A few dozen rows, so one page of requests.
rows.vgi.example_queries: [{"description": "Which stories are gaining activity right now", "sql": "SELECT title, score, descendants AS comments FROM hackernews.main.updated_items WHERE type = 'story' ORDER BY score DESC"}]
rows.vgi.title: Recently Changed Items

rows: CREATE TABLE updated_items(rank INTEGER NOT NULL, id BIGINT, "type" VARCHAR, author VARCHAR, created_at TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE, title VARCHAR, url VARCHAR, "text" VARCHAR, score BIGINT, descendants BIGINT, parent BIGINT, poll BIGINT, kids BIGINT[], parts BIGINT[], deleted BOOLEAN, dead BOOLEAN, UNIQUE(rank), PRIMARY KEY(id));
The Hacker News front page ranking: up to 500 stories and job ads, in the order the site shows them

rows.vgi.doc_llm: What is on the Hacker News front page right now, in ranked order — the place to start for 'what is the tech world talking about today'. Rank 1 is the top slot and ranks 1-30 are the site's first page. Job ads are ranked here too; filter `type = 'story'` to drop them. Each `id` opens the story's discussion via `comments()`.
rows.vgi.doc_md:
The ranking behind the site's home page, up to 500 deep.

### What decides the order

Hacker News ranks by votes, decayed by age, and adjusted by moderators and flags — so a lower-scored new story can sit above a higher-scored old one. `rank` is the site's order; `score` is only one input to it.

### Cost

Rows stream in rank order, 100 per batch and one request per story, so a `LIMIT` reads only what it returns; an `ORDER BY` reads the whole list first.
rows.vgi.example_queries: [{"description": "The first page of Hacker News, stories only", "sql": "SELECT rank, title, score, descendants AS comments FROM hackernews.main.top_stories WHERE type = 'story' ORDER BY rank LIMIT 30"}]
rows.vgi.title: Front Page

rows: CREATE TABLE top_stories(rank INTEGER NOT NULL, id BIGINT, "type" VARCHAR, author VARCHAR, created_at TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE, title VARCHAR, url VARCHAR, "text" VARCHAR, score BIGINT, descendants BIGINT, parent BIGINT, poll BIGINT, kids BIGINT[], parts BIGINT[], deleted BOOLEAN, dead BOOLEAN, UNIQUE(rank), PRIMARY KEY(id));
Ask HN questions currently listed, as the Ask HN page ranks them

rows.vgi.doc_llm: The Ask HN questions the site's 'ask' page lists right now: members asking the community for advice, opinions or experiences. These are text posts — the question is in `text` (HTML) and `url` is NULL — and the answers are the discussion, which `comments()` returns.
rows.vgi.doc_md:
Up to 200 Ask HN posts, in the ranking of the site's 'ask' page; usually far fewer.

### Reading a question

An Ask HN post has no link: its body is in `text`, as HTML. Decode it with `html_to_text()`. Its answers are the thread under its `id`.

### Cost

Rows stream in rank order, 100 per batch and one request per story, so a `LIMIT` reads only what it returns; an `ORDER BY` reads the whole list first.
rows.vgi.example_queries: [{"description": "The Ask HN questions drawing the most answers", "sql": "SELECT title, descendants AS answers, hackernews.main.html_to_text(text) AS question FROM hackernews.main.ask_stories ORDER BY answers DESC LIMIT 10"}]
rows.vgi.title: Ask HN

rows: CREATE TABLE ask_stories(rank INTEGER NOT NULL, id BIGINT, "type" VARCHAR, author VARCHAR, created_at TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE, title VARCHAR, url VARCHAR, "text" VARCHAR, score BIGINT, descendants BIGINT, parent BIGINT, poll BIGINT, kids BIGINT[], parts BIGINT[], deleted BOOLEAN, dead BOOLEAN, UNIQUE(rank), PRIMARY KEY(id));
Hacker News' 'best' list: the highest-voted recent stories

rows.vgi.doc_llm: The highest-voted stories of the last few days, as the site's 'best' page ranks them. Reach for it for 'what did people like most this week', where the front page answers 'what is hot this hour'. Scores here run far higher than on the front page.
rows.vgi.doc_md:
Hacker News' 'best' ranking — highest-voted recent links — typically 200 stories deep.

### Versus the front page

The front page decays by age hour to hour; this list holds on to the strongest stories for days. Join the two on `id` to see which of today's front-page stories are also among the week's best.

### Cost

Rows stream in rank order, 100 per batch and one request per story, so a `LIMIT` reads only what it returns; an `ORDER BY` reads the whole list first.
rows.vgi.example_queries: [{"description": "The ten highest-scoring stories of the last few days", "sql": "SELECT title, score, descendants AS comments FROM hackernews.main.best_stories ORDER BY score DESC LIMIT 10"}]
rows.vgi.title: Highest-Voted Recent Stories

rows: CREATE TABLE best_stories(rank INTEGER NOT NULL, id BIGINT, "type" VARCHAR, author VARCHAR, created_at TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE, title VARCHAR, url VARCHAR, "text" VARCHAR, score BIGINT, descendants BIGINT, parent BIGINT, poll BIGINT, kids BIGINT[], parts BIGINT[], deleted BOOLEAN, dead BOOLEAN, UNIQUE(rank), PRIMARY KEY(id));
The 500 most recently submitted Hacker News stories, newest first

rows.vgi.doc_llm: The latest submissions to Hacker News, newest first, before voting has sorted them — what the site's 'new' page shows. Use it to catch a story the moment it is posted, or to see what is being submitted rather than what is popular. Most rows have a score of one or two; that is the point of the list.
rows.vgi.doc_md:
Up to 500 of the most recent submissions, in the order the 'new' page lists them.

### Turnover

New stories arrive every minute or so and the list holds roughly the last ten hours of them, so two reads a few minutes apart overlap only partly. Poll it, keyed on `id`, to follow everything submitted.

### Cost

Rows stream in rank order, 100 per batch and one request per story, so a `LIMIT` reads only what it returns; an `ORDER BY` reads the whole list first.
rows.vgi.example_queries: [{"description": "The newest submissions that are already drawing votes", "sql": "SELECT title, author, score, created_at FROM hackernews.main.new_stories WHERE score > 1 ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT 20"}]
rows.vgi.title: Newest Submissions

rows: CREATE TABLE new_stories(rank INTEGER NOT NULL, id BIGINT, "type" VARCHAR, author VARCHAR, created_at TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE, title VARCHAR, url VARCHAR, "text" VARCHAR, score BIGINT, descendants BIGINT, parent BIGINT, poll BIGINT, kids BIGINT[], parts BIGINT[], deleted BOOLEAN, dead BOOLEAN, UNIQUE(rank), PRIMARY KEY(id));
